item.title: Report says Jewish family felt they were driven out of Kerry
item.description: A report on anti-Semitism in Ireland will include details of a Jewish family who said they felt they had to leave Kerry because of their identity. The Jewish Representative Council of Ireland is compiling the report which will be published in the new year. The report will include the views of a US Jewish family who had been living in Killorglin for five years. item.title: PSG ordered to pay Mbappe 60 million euro
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain have been ordered to pay former player Kylian Mbappe 60 million euros. He'd taken the European champions to court in France after claiming they owed him more than 263-million euros in unpaid salary and bonuses. The striker moved from P-S-G to Real Madrid on a free transfer last year. Advertisement

item.title: Okwute signs new contract with Kerry FC
item.description: Kerry FC has confirmed that Daniel Okwute has signed a new deal with the Kingdom for 2026. Since joining in the summer of 2023 the 22 year-old Killarney native has made 80 appearances, scoring 7 goals and assisting on 15 occasions. item.title: Bree appointed Head of Player Pathway Coaching and Content
item.description: Michael Bree has been appointed Basketball Ireland’s Head of Player Pathway Coaching and Content with the Irish U14, U15 and U17 Academies. Bree, who took over as Ireland senior men’s head coach in September, has an extensive track record in player development, through his role as Programme Director at RIG Mark Basketball, which he has held since 2014, developing elite level international players for Sweden’s men’s and women’s teams. item.title: Ireland lose to South Africa
item.description: The Ireland women's cricketers suffered a 74-run defeat in their second one-day international against South Africa. The hosts set a target of 376 runs after 50 overs, before the tourists were bowled out for 301, with Orla Prendergast coming up just short of a century at bat. The two sides will meet for the final match in Johannesburg on Friday. Advertisement

item.title: Soutar advances after sudden-death leg
item.description: At the PDC World Darts Championship in London, Scottish thrower Alan Soutar needed a sudden-death leg in the deciding set to get the better of Finland's Teemu Harju. World number eight Chris Dobey is also through to the second round, after 3-1 win over China's Xiao Chen Zong. Former champion Gerwyn Price will be among those in action tonight when he plays Adam Gawlas. Advertisement

item.title: Kerry Dairy Ireland drops November milk price by further 3.5c/l
item.description: Kerry Dairy Ireland has dropped its November milk price by a further 3.5 cent per litre (c/l), reflecting the ongoing trend among milk processors nationwide. It will now pay 37.5 c/l including VAT and quality and sustainability bonuses for milk supplied by farmers last month. In its monthly statement, the milk processor said the outlook for prices remains weak globally, as the milk supply continues to grow at an unprecedented pace. item.title: Fire brought under control in Listowel
item.description: Two units of Kerry Fire and Rescue Service attended a blaze in Listowel this afternoon. Emergency services were notified at around 3pm of the fire at College Cross Apartments on the Ballygologue Road. Listowel and Ballybunion fire units attended the scene along with gardaí and the ambulance service. Advertisement The units brought the fire under control.

item.title: West Kerry Community Hospital now operating at full capacity with opening of final two beds
item.description: The HSE says West Kerry Community Hospital is now operating at its full capacity with the opening of more beds in recent days. The lack of available bedspace at the centre for older people near Dingle, has been highlighted by local representatives. The current capacity of the centre is 46 residents, and the HSE says all 46 beds are now operational, with the last two beds having opened today. item.title: United captain claims club 'wanted him to leave'
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes claims the club 'wanted him to leave' for a huge fee in the summer. Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal were reportedly prepared to pay 100-million pounds to land the midfielder. The 31-year-old - who's played more than 300 games since joining United in 2020 - told a Portuguese TV channel the club said he could go, which "hurt" him. Advertisement
